targets.baseline_commit_message: keep-a-record-library-valid: the launch-video delivery gate, byte copies (first commit of a port)

preserve: every routed MUST check of the stages needs a pass row (per option for per-option checks); advisory passes only at a stage its check names
a machine row counts only with the reviewed pin of what measured it; an agent cannot write a machine name
a row on other bytes than its file pins (or, without pins, recorded before the file changed) is unanswered
one cause, one row: the copy row counts every finding but the person's verdict rows, the verdict row only those
audit-watch holds every linked file whose option has an open or failed row, never a superseded round or a row waiting on the person
allowed_deltas: every name of one library (files, folders, patterns, stages, rule ids, fact layouts, limits) is the schema's delivery_gate
the copy check is tools/check-against-a-persons-rules-and-verdicts check-a-films-copy.mjs, reading the person's branch through their records door; its pin is its code and the branch rows as read
the render check is tools/check-a-rendered-video beside this tool; its limits a setting or an argument
the start of an investigation is the tool's own investigation.start; the header and routes are routes.py
the output keys and words that named the person become waits_for_the_person and the person
banned_substitutions: a second copy of this job in another folder
a person's name, film, path or rule file written in code
a frozen copy of the person's verdict rows
_paths: The source lives in a private repository, so it is named by the BLAKE3 identity of its path (path_multihash, tools/content-investigation/cis.py); a checkout of trillion-launch-video beside this one finds it.
